ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The primary statutes governing UBO/AML compliance are the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 11389, as amended), Articles 2 and 5-2, and its Enforcement Decree; the Financial Services Commission Regulation on the Identification of Beneficial Owners and Verification of Customers; the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality; the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Articles 17, 18, 23, 24, 289 and 543; and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for inbound investment reporting. Korea also follows FATF recommendations and UN Security Council resolutions through the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit. Beneficial owners holding 25% or more are identified and reported to banks and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit; there is no public UBO register, and the information is accessible to competent authorities only.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registration Office (court registry) of the Korean incorporated entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: court-issued certified extract plus apostille by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Apostille Division. Consular path: no apostille; use Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs certificate followed by legalization by the destination country's embassy or consulate in Korea. The two paths are mutually exclusive and never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certified Corporate Registration Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registration Office where the company is registered
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: certified registry extract plus apostille by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Non-Hague destination: Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs certificate followed by consular legalization by the destination state; never both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Parent company board of directors and corporate representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention state: notarized board resolution or power of attorney plus apostille from the competent authority of the country of origin, then use in Korea without Korean consular steps. Non-Hague state: notarization plus legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate in the country of origin. No sequential apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public and the incorporators of the Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For use abroad: notarized by Korean notary public plus apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For use in Korea from a foreign incorporator: apostille from the foreign competent authority if that country is a Hague member; otherwise consular legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate. Parallel paths only.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank maintaining the shareholder or UBO relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: When issued in a Hague member state: bank letter on original letterhead, notarization of the bank officer's signature, and apostille by that state's competent authority. When issued in a non-Hague state: notarization and Korean consular legalization. A Korean bank letter must bear the bank's corporate seal and Korean MOFA apostille when used abroad. Never chain apostille and consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every proposed shareholder, UBO, director and signatory must be screened before incorporation against the OFAC SDN List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Republic of Korea's designated-person list administered by the Financial Services Commission and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit. Screening must include fuzzy and alias matching, and all positive results trigger enhanced due diligence. PEPs, family members and close associates require source-of-wealth verification and senior management approval. Screening records must be retained for at least five years and produced to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit upon request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: IROS - Internet Registration Office System of the Supreme Court of Korea (https://iros.srt.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be written in Korean Hangul and may include Latin letters, Arabic numerals, and certain punctuation. The legal form suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa' must appear in the statutory name. The registry uses graphic and phonetic similarity checks, including transliteration of foreign names into Hangul, to prevent confusion with existing companies. A parallel English trade name may be registered but the Korean statutory name controls for registration rights.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the IROS search indicates a conflict with an existing registered name, the applicant should file a revised name through the same portal; there is no statutory extension of the 30-day pre-clearance, but a fresh pre-clearance request may be submitted. If the registration court issues a formal rejection order, the applicant may file an objection within 14 days under Article 5 of the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. The court reviews written evidence and may hold a hearing; its ruling can be appealed under Article 6 of the same Act. Rejections based on sensitive tokens require prior ministerial approval and cannot be cured by appeal alone.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A stand-alone virtual office or commercial mailbox address is not accepted for the statutory registered office of a Yuhan Hoesa because the Commercial Act requires the headquarters to be located at the registered office, and the National Tax Service requires a real place of business for business registration. For an ISIC 5222 ship crew recruitment agency, the Seafarers Act and maritime crew licensing rules require a physical office with employment records, personnel equipment, and a compliance manager. Korean banks reject virtual offices for corporate account opening and require a physical site visit. A serviced or executive office is acceptable only if the company has exclusive occupation, a reception area, employee presence, and all books and records available for inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: physical office and lease, company sign and workplace equipment, original certificate of incorporation and license, seafarer employment contracts, personnel records and voucher files, payroll and tax records, AML/CFT files, compliance officer availability, and access for National Tax Service officers and Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries inspectors. Quantified risk: an unannounced site inspection is 70% likely for a licensed crew recruitment agency within the first 12 months; the National Tax Service audits approximately 30% of new maritime service companies; banks conduct a mandatory physical inspection in 100% of operating account openings before activation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 15252, as amended), Part IV Limited Liability Company, Articles 287-2 through 287-74; Commercial Registration Act and its Enforcement Decree; Supreme Court Registration Procedures; Foreign Investment Promotion Act where a non-resident owns equity.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Civil Registration Section, District Court located at the principal Korean registered office; for Seoul, Seoul Central District Court Registry; after incorporation, the competent District Tax Office of the National Tax Service for business registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa), accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, paid-in capital certificate, registered seal specimen, consent of appointed manager/directors and auditor, proof of registered office, and all required court registration schedules.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None required under the Korean Commercial Act; a Yuhan Hoesa may be formed with nominal or zero stated minimum capital and no blocked escrow account is mandated. The members must nevertheless pay or contribute all subscribed capital before the establishment registration is filed, and the registry will require bank confirmation or an in-kind valuation certificate. If foreign investment is involved, the funds must be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and may be temporarily held in a foreign-investment bank account until the incorporation is registered, but that is not a statutory capital escrow.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: We, the undersigned initial members and first directors of the [legal entity name] Yuhan Hoesa (the Company), acting at the founding meeting duly convened on [date], adopt the following Pro-Forma First Board Resolution with full authority and confirm all actions of the incorporators. RESOLVED, that the notarized Articles of Incorporation of the Company, recorded as [article no.], are approved and ratified; the total share capital of the Company is established at [currency amount], divided into [number] non-par-value equities, all of which have been validly subscribed by the members named in the subscriber list; the representative manager is directed to collect and bank all capital contributions, and the capital contribution account certificate shall be delivered to the registry. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be located at [address in Korea], and the representative manager is authorized to execute and deliver the office lease, to present the leasehold consent certificate to the registry and the National Tax Service, and to make any subsequent relocation filings. RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed as the representative director / managing director of the Company, and [name] is appointed as the statutory auditor or non-auditor observer, in accordance with the Articles; each officer shall possess the authority granted by Article [x] of the Articles and the Commercial Act, including exclusive authority for maritime crew recruitment business filings, banking, tax filings, and execution of all contracts related to crew management. RESOLVED, that the Company shall open operating and payroll accounts with [bank], including SWIFT wire and multi-currency payroll facilities, and the representative director, together with one second signatory, are jointly authorized to issue wire instructions, sign account mandates and receive bank cards for operational use. RESOLVED, that the Company adopt the corporate seal, register the seal with the district court and tax office, and appoint counsel to file the incorporation registration, business registration, and the maritime seafarer recruitment and placement license under the Seafarers Act. RESOLVED, that all actions taken before the date of this resolution by the promoters, including the subscription agreements and banking instructions, be and they are hereby ratified, confirmed, and adopted as corporate acts. This resolution is effective from the date of its adoption and supersedes all conflicting resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, Articles of Incorporation, Notarization and Capital Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean civil notary public in the judicial district of the registered office; corporate name search database of the Supreme Court of Korea; designated foreign exchange bank for capital contribution receipt.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name search in the Supreme Court registration database for the exact Korean name and English transliteration containing the legal suffix Yuhan Hoesa. Prepare the notarized Articles of Incorporation in the Korean language, stating corporate name, business purpose covering maritime seafarer staffing, crew management, recruitment agency and marine support services, registered office, total capital, subscription method, number of equity interests, authorized directors, auditor, duration, fiscal year, and reporting provisions. Have all founding members sign or seal the articles, then arrange notarization by a Korean civil notary public. Before notarization, deposit all subscription amounts into a temporary capital collection account or obtain bank confirmation of the in-kind contribution valuation. Foreign members must supply apostilled passports, proof of address, and a foreign nationality declaration. After notarization, retain a Korean law firm to coordinate the next registry submission and secure a certified Korean translation of any foreign public documents.
required_dossiers: Apostilled or legalized passport copies of all members
Proof of residential or shareholder address
Draft notarized Articles of Incorporation
Subscription statement and equity allocation schedule
Written consents of the appointed directors/manager and auditor
Corporate name search confirmation
Power of attorney authorizing Korean counsel to file
Temporary capital contribution account certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or name search marks a query, correct the inconsistency in the draft Articles, re-notarize the corrected instrument, or select a new permissible company name. If a foreign document is challenged, obtain a fresh apostille, certified translation, and re-submit before the statutory correction window closes; if the notary refuses, use another Korean notary public in the same judicial district.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: District Court Registration of Incorporation and Corporate Seal Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Section of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office; electronic filing through the Supreme Court e-ROKEIS system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Application for Establishment Registration of a Limited Liability Company with the Commercial Registration Section after capital payment is verified. Submit the notarized Articles, subscription schedule, capital receipt certificate or in-kind valuation, registered office leasehold consent certificate, consent documents of the representative manager and auditor, personal seal certificates of the directors and auditor, registered corporate seal specimen, and foreign member apostilles. The court registrar examines the statutory requirements under the Commercial Act and Registration Rules. Pay the registration tax and local education tax assessed on declared capital according to the applicable schedule. Once the registrar accepts the filing, the court issues the corporate registration certificate, certified corporate registry, and seal registration certificate. Legal personality is created on the registration date, and the corporate seal should be registered with the same court before signing operational agreements.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company
Notarized Articles of Incorporation signed or sealed by all members
Certificate of paid-up capital or in-kind contribution valuation
Bank receipt or capital deposit certificate
Registered office lease and landlord consent certificate
List of members and subscription amounts
Consent to appointment of directors/manager and auditor
Personal seal certificates and certified identity documents of officers
Corporate seal specimen and seal registration form
Power of attorney from the company to filing counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or suspended, submit the requested supplementary evidence within the court correction period, usually 14 days. If the registration is rejected, cure the stated formal defects, file a corrected fresh application, or request administrative appeal through the local court panel having jurisdiction over commercial registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service Business Registration and Tax Permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent District Tax Office of the National Tax Service; electronic filing through Home Tax e-Service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an application for business registration with the district tax office within the statutory period after incorporation. Provide the corporate registration certificate, notarized Articles, office lease, corporate seal certificate, director identity documents, bank account data, and registered office premises consent. Indicate the principal business as crew recruitment and ship manning services for corporate tax, value added tax, payroll withholding, and electronic tax invoice purposes. The tax office will issue the Business Registration Certificate containing the Korean corporate number and tax classification. If no Korean resident officer is available, appoint a domestic tax representative before filing the first periodic returns. After receiving the Business Registration Certificate, activate VAT invoicing, set up payroll tax schedules, and maintain the registered address for receipt of tax notices and correspondence.
required_dossiers: Corporate Registration Certificate issued by the district court
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Business Registration Application Form
Office lease agreement and consent of the owner
Corporate seal registration certificate
Identity documents of the representative director
Registered office title or lease consent proof
Bank account details and foreign exchange bank confirmation
Tax representative appointment letter if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office issues a query, supply the missing lease consent or correct the business site information and re-file through Home Tax. If registration is refused, provide a signed correction letter, request a site inspection, or file an administrative review before the National Tax Service review committee within 90 days of the adverse decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Report, Corporate Banking and Multi-Currency Payroll Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: KOTRA Foreign Investment Support Center, licensed Korean foreign exchange bank, Financial Supervisory Service through the bank for AML due diligence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If a non-resident owns equity in the Yuhan Hoesa, file the foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act before or immediately after subscription of the equity interests. Submit the report at KOTRA or through a designated foreign exchange bank, and obtain the Certificate of Foreign Investment after the inbound remittance is booked. Open a foreign-investment account, receive the contributed funds, and then transfer or convert the funds to the operating corporate account after the court registration is complete. Complete customer due diligence at the bank with AML/KYC forms, beneficial ownership declaration, source of funds evidence, and intended transaction profile for SWIFT wires and multi-currency payroll. Execute banking mandates for two-signatory wire approval and set up segregated payroll sub-accounts for seafarer wage payments in multiple currencies. Retain all remittance and conversion records for corporate tax and foreign exchange compliance.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Report Form
Passport and proof of nationality of foreign members
Certificate of Foreign Investment
Bank remittance receipts and source of funds declaration
Corporate Registration Certificate and Business Registration Certificate
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Foreign exchange transaction report forms
AML and beneficial ownership declarations
Board resolution approving bank mandates and payroll accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the foreign investment report is rejected, coordinate with KOTRA and the bank to correct the remittance classification and refile. If the bank asks for enhanced due diligence, supply documented source of funds, corporate structure charts, and vessel or client contracts. If a foreign exchange violation is alleged, respond with an explanatory statement and administrative appeal under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act before the Ministry of Economy and Finance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries Crew Recruitment Agency License and Operational Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Regional Maritime Affairs Office of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries; Ministry of Employment and Labor for occupational safety; local district office and fire authority for commercial premises clearance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the regional Maritime Affairs Office for the Seafarer Recruitment and Placement Agency Registration required under the Seafarers Act and its Enforcement Decree for ISIC 5222 crew recruitment and manning agency operations. Submit a detailed business plan covering crew recruitment, vessel crew management, placement procedures, employment agreement templates, advances and payroll policies, seafarer insurance, and welfare arrangements. Provide office facility evidence, corporate registration, business registration, responsible-person background certificates, and proof of professional indemnity or occupational accident insurance. The Ministry may conduct an on-site inspection and verify that the agency does not charge prohibited recruitment fees to seafarers. After approval, display the license in the office and comply with annual reporting, seafarer registration, and mandatory record-keeping. If placing foreign seafarers on Korean-controlled vessels, maintain passport, visa, crew list, and flag-state manning documentation accessible for inspection at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Seafarer Recruitment and Placement Agency Registration Application
Business plan and crew recruitment procedure manual
Corporate Registration Certificate
Business Registration Certificate
Office lease contract and premises layout
Employment agreement and dispatch contract templates
Insurance policies covering occupational accidents and liability
Criminal background certificates of responsible officers
Seafarer welfare and compensation policy
Annual compliance report templates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries issues a deficiency notice, correct each item and respond within the stated cure period. If the license is denied, request an administrative adjudication before the Korean Maritime Administration and simultaneously submit a revised application curing all facility, insurance, and labor protection deficiencies.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (The Central Bank of the Republic of Korea)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a highly liberalized foreign exchange control regime governed by the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with Bank of Korea and the Ministry of Economy and Finance exercising regulatory oversight. Current account transactions such as trade settlements, seafarer payroll remittances, and profit dividends are generally freely permitted upon submission of supporting documentation. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity injections and external borrowing, require prior notification, declaration, or post-transaction reporting to the Foreign Exchange Information System, administered by Korea Customs Service. The Korean won is fully convertible for bona fide current account operations, but the government retains policy tools to impose temporary countermeasures during extraordinary volatility. Export proceeds are not subject to a mandatory surrender ratio, but every receipt must be reported and physically collectible within the statutory settlement period. Profit remittance hurdles are relatively low for a resident Korean limited liability company, providing the entity maintains audited financial statements, corporate tax clearance certificates, and underlying commercial or payroll service contracts. The overarching compliance burden is documentary rather than restrictive, with banks acting as the front-line reporting agents. This regime is therefore assessable as business-friendly for a crew recruitment agency, provided all underlying maritime employment service agreements are free of sanctions and flag-state violations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be collected within twelve months from the date of the original export declaration, extendable by up to two years upon approved justification. There is no mandatory conversion percentage to Korean won; export foreign currency receipts may be credited in full to a domestic foreign currency account or converted at the exporter's discretion. The receipt must be reported to the Foreign Exchange Information System within thirty days to maintain regulatory transparency.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border fintech EMIs such as Revolut, Wise, or Airwallex are not licensed as deposit-taking banks by the Financial Supervisory Service and are legally barred from providing domestic Korean-won corporate transactional accounts or payroll clearing services to a resident Korean entity. They may function only as ancillary remittance aggregators or payment facilitators bridging account holders to licensed Korean banks. They cannot be considered a viable primary treasury rail for a Yuhan Hoesa operating in South Korea. The optimal approach is to maintain operational treasury accounts at a tier-1 domestic commercial bank and use the EMI only for spot foreign-currency conversion if the EMI is backed by a licensed overseas bank and the underlying data flow satisfies the bank's audit trail requirements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean Financial Supervisory Service regulations generally permit non-face-to-face corporate account opening through certified digital identity authentication. However, most tier-1 commercial banks impose a mandatory in-branch identification and compliance interview for at least one statutory director or a formally appointed proxy holder with a notarized power of attorney. Remote consular proxy opening is not universally accepted; the bank's Local Compliance Unit must pre-approve any remote video interview. For a foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa, the full beneficial ownership chain must be attested and the bank may demand that the ultimate beneficial owner appear by video if the statutory director cannot present physically in Seoul.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between the registered legal representative in the Korean company registry and the actual beneficial owner listed in the AML declaration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry extract, a fully completed beneficial ownership schedule, valid passports and alien registration cards of all directors and UBOs, a notarized board resolution appointing the account signatories, and a stamped ownership-chain chart evidencing each intermediate entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the initial capital escrow and anticipated seafarer payroll deposits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of bank transaction statements from the beneficiary owner's source-account, certified audited or management financial statements, executed crew management agreements, payroll projection spreadsheets, and a written capital source declaration countersigned by the compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential sanctions exposure due to vessel flags, trading routes, or seafarer nationalities within the crew recruitment agency's portfolio.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete IMO and flag registry of vessels under management, a full crew roster with passport copies, an OFAC and UN sanctions screening report, deployment contracts, charter party agreements, and a signed sanctions compliance attestation confirming no operations with Iran, North Korea, Syria, Cuba, or Crimea-registered vessels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pattern of recurring cross-border payroll remittances to offshore seafarers flagged as structurally similar to shell-company disbursement behavior.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Individual seafarer employment agreements, bi-colour reconciled payroll records, a Philippine or other third-country manning agency partnership certificate where applicable, crew passports, time-and-attendance records, and annual corporate tax filings or withholding tax certificates matching the wired amounts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital must be routed through a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank after the foreign investor files an FDI report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The remitting bank will apply a purpose code for capital contribution on the SWIFT MT103. The funds should be credited to a dedicated Capital Escrow Account and then transferred to the Basic Operational Currency Account only after the Korean bank receives the foreign investment notification certificate and the external auditor completes a capital verification memo. Any require amount in excess of the declared foreign investment is blocked until the surplus is reported and legalized.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound seafarer wages and crew management service fees are settled through SWIFT MT103 payments, Commercial Documentary Collections, or standby Letters of Credit when requested by the foreign client. Domestic clearing for Korean-sourced disbursements flows through the Korean Won wire network via the Bank of Korea's CLS-adjacent settlement infrastructure. For cross-border payroll, each MT103 transmission must include the underlying invoice or payroll schedule and the appropriate service-payment purpose code so the receiving bank sees a transparent trade-services trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts with licensed Korean banks for receivables and payables up to twelve months tenor
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on the Korean won executed through a domestic bank's NDF desk only for hedging non-KRW trade or payroll exposures
Cross-currency swaps limited to amortizing ship-owner working capital lines and crew payroll programs, expressly prohibited for speculative arbitrage without underlying commercial exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and final tax settlement for the preceding fiscal year under the Corporate Income Tax Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 immediately following the close of the fiscal year if the fiscal year ends on December 31; for any other fiscal year-end, the last day of the third month after the fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or underreporting attracts an additional tax of 20% of the underpaid amount (40% for malicious or grossly negligent underreporting), a late-filing surcharge of 10% of the tax payable, and statutory interest at the Bank of Korea base rate plus 3.5 percentage points per annum from the due date to the payment date. Persistent default can result in compulsory asset collection and administrative closure of the tax registration, with consequential revocation or non-renewal of the maritime crew recruitment licence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local corporation income tax return and payment for the preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government tax authority (si/gun/gu) at the company's registered seat
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following the close of the fiscal year (three-month window from the fiscal year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or non-payment accrues local tax delinquency charges at the prescribed monthly rate (approximately 0.75% per month for up to 36 months), suspension of tax clearance certificates, compulsory collection against corporate assets, and loss of good-standing certificates required for governmental vessel crew agency approvals.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax return for each six-month tax period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (VAT tax office of the registered seat)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For the first half of the calendar year: on or before July 25 of that year. For the second half of the calendar year: on or before January 25 of the following year. If the fiscal year is not the calendar year, the deadline is within 25 days after each six-month corporate VAT tax period closes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or misdeclaration gives rise to VAT penalties of up to 10% of the unpaid VAT, per-day late penalties at statutory rates, and loss of input VAT credits where receipts are defective; continued failure subjects the company to assessment by the NTS, seizure of bank accounts, and strike-off from the business registration list for maritime payroll operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary general meeting of members for approval of statutory financial statements and ratification of directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate governance body; minutes and resolutions must be retained at the registered office and made available for inspection by members, NTS, and court authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending December 31, the annual ordinary general meeting of members must be convened within three months after the fiscal year-end, i.e., by March 31; earlier date if required in the articles of incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the meeting within the statutory window renders the representative director liable to administrative fines and disqualifying actions; members may apply to the court for judicial dissolution of the company is not cured, and the absence of approved audited financial statements will cause the corporate tax filing and the maritime licence renewal to be rejected.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and renewal of the maritime seafarer recruitment and crew management agency licence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries of the Republic of Korea (Maritime Transport Policy Bureau)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days before each licence anniversary date; the licence does not automatically renew if the required annual employer/seafarer placement records, beneficial ownership update, and statutory financial statements are not submitted in the prescribed form.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Expiry or non-renewal automatically lapses the licence, prohibits the company from recruiting or placing seafarers on Korean-flag vessels, attracts administrative fines for unlicensed agency operations, and may lead to facility closure orders and referral to the prosecutors for operating without the statutory licence.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit and Accounting, an independent audit by a certified public accountant is mandatory for (i) all listed Korean companies; (ii) all financial investment companies and financial institutions; and (iii) any other Korean incorporated entity, including a Yuhan Hoesa limited liability company, whose total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 8.9 million). The law does not impose a general separate turnover or headcount audit threshold for a private LLC, but a maritime crew agency may be required by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries to obtain a CPA audit as a licence-renewal condition where annual payroll handled exceeds 1,000 seafarers or where annual foreign-currency remittances exceed KRW 15,000,000,000 (approximately USD 11.2 million). The quantitative triggers are therefore balance-sheet assets of KRW 12 billion or more, enhanced payroll/remittance operating thresholds for maritime licence continuation, and any designation as a public-interest company by the Financial Services Commission.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korea International Financial Reporting Standards) for entities that are listed, in the financial sector, or voluntarily electing IFRS; otherwise Korean GAAP (General Corporate Accounting Standards) for non-listed private companies such as a Yuhan Hoesa. Regardless of the accounting framework, all statutory financial statements must be audited under Korean Generally Accepted Auditing Standards when the audit threshold is met, and must be approved by the general meeting of members.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not currently maintain a general annual UBO registry for private domestic LLCs. The Yuhan Hoesa is required to keep an up-to-date register of members at its registered office, and any transfer of membership quota or change in beneficial ownership must be reflected in that register contemporaneously. If a transfer causes a change in the registered corporate information (for example, transfer of all quota or appointment of a new representative), a court registration amendment must be filed within three weeks of the transfer. In addition, under Korean anti-money-laundering law, financial institutions are required to obtain and report beneficial ownership information to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) for every company account; the maritime crew agency must also disclose its controlling members to the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries at each licence renewal, including any increase in foreign ownership. There is no separate 30-day UBO confirmation return to a company registry, but ownership changes must be updated internally and must be filed with the court within the three-week statutory registration window.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Auditors (if an auditor is appointed)
Register of Charges and Mortgages over company assets
Minute Book of general meetings of members
Book of financial statements and supporting accounting records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - USD 2,000 per year for a compliant corporate registered office and company secretarial agent; USD 1,000 - USD 3,200 per year if bookkeeping, payroll, and tax-agency services are bundled for the crew staffing operation.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 15,000 for a full K-IFRS statutory audit once the KRW 12 billion balance-sheet threshold is reached; USD 3,000 - USD 7,000 for an agreed-upon financial review for a smaller private company with less than 200 seafarers on payroll.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Progressive rate: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% on KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% on KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; 24% on excess over KRW 300 billion
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory incentives include: research and development (R&D) super-deductions, tax credits for job creation and facility investment, special Free Economic Zone (FEZ) tax exemptions/reductions for foreign-invested companies, and patent box-style regime for qualifying intellectual property income

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (법인세과세표준 및 세액계산서) designated as NTS Form No. 101, filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The corporate tax return must be filed within 3 months from the end of the fiscal year-end (e.g., for a December 31 year-end, the deadline is March 31 of the following year). Intermediate (prepayments) are due within 2 months of the first half fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross sales and revenue from crew recruitment, crewing management, and vessel manning services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders and foreign enterprises must ensure that all revenue attributable to South Korean sourcing and local operations is fully reported. Any allocation to offshore entities must be supported by transfer pricing documentation evidencing arm's length compensation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income excluded from taxable corporate income, such as certain foreign-source dividends qualifying for participation exemption or income subject to tax incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate owners cannot claim exemption on repatriated profits or offshore crew payroll fees unless the income is demonstrated as having no Korean situs, or the applicable tax treaty provides exclusive residence-state taxing rights. A strict nexus analysis is required to avoid under-reporting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additions (and deductions) arising from cross-border related-party transactions with foreign affiliates, including management fees and service charges for crew sourcing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The filing entity must attach an arm's length adjustment schedule for any intercompany service fee, commission, or payroll cost charged by or to a non-resident affiliate. Korean tax officers may impute income if the foreign counterparty lacks actual economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit claimed for foreign income taxes paid on worldwide or Korean-source income (depending on residence classification).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies limited to Korean-source taxation should only claim foreign tax credits if the income is also taxable in Korea under domestic law and the treaty. Documentation must include foreign tax returns and payment receipts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 23 - Tax Base and Rate Calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable progressive corporate income tax rate applied to the net taxable income after deductions and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities without a Korean permanent establishment (PE) are not subject to Korean corporate tax on business income, but are subject to final withholding tax on Korean-source dividends, interest, royalties, and certain service fees. If a PE exists, this box must be completed on a net basis using the same entity's global allocation methodology.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for R&D, job creation, and Free Economic Zone investments, which may reduce the final corporate income tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-controlled entities may claim these incentives only if the qualifying activity is carried out in Korea and the underlying investment has real fixed-place-of-business substance. Any incentive claimed must align with the OECD BEPS Action Plan 5 substantial-activity requirement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: 20% of unpaid corporate tax if filed within 1 month of the statutory deadline; 30% if filed after 1 month; 40% if filed after 2 months; 50% if filed after 3 months. In addition, an overdue payment surcharge of 0.022% per day (approximately 8.03% annually) applies. Criminal fraud penalties: under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, wilful omission or false declaration can result in imprisonment of up to 3 years (10 years for evasion exceeding KRW 3 billion) and fines up to 3 times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wHT_rate: 20% national withholding tax on Korean-source dividends paid to non-resident corporations, plus an additional 2% local income tax surcharge, resulting in a combined effective rate of 22% before treaty relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke bilateral Double Tax Agreement (DTA) relief on outbound dividends, interest or royalties, the non-resident recipient must submit: (i) an application for treaty reduction under Article 62-2 of the Framework Act for National Taxes (Form IR-21), (ii) a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) duly apostilled or certified by the tax authority of the residence state, (iii) a beneficial ownership statement confirming that the non-resident is the actual recipient and has the right to enjoy the income (not an intermediary, conduit or bare nominee), and (iv) if applicable, the relevant DTA articles and a claim form for reduced withholding rate. The application must be filed with the tax withholding agent before the payment date, or, in cases where the withholding has already been applied at full statutory rate, a refund claim may be filed with the local District Tax Office within the statutory prescription period (generally 3 years).

stage_6.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: interest and royalty payments to non-residents are subject to 20% national withholding plus 2% local surcharge, equalling 22% combined. Under most Korean tax treaties, the rate may be reduced to 0% to 15% on interest and 0% to 10% on royalties, depending on the treaty partner and beneficial ownership status. An application for treaty application must be filed using Form IR-21 together with the non-resident's TRC and beneficial ownership evidence.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File documentation is mandatory when the aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions exceeds KRW 50 billion (approximately USD 40 million) in a fiscal year; Master File documentation is required when the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds KRW 1 trillion (approximately USD 800 million).
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) in Korea apply via judicial anti-avoidance doctrines and the Substance over Form rule. For free-zone or tax-holiday entities, the actual performance of Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in Korea, such as decision-making, management, crew payroll administration, and client contracting, must be verifiable. In transfer pricing audits, the Korean tax authority also applies the OECD BEPS Action Plan 6/8 principles to recharacterize transactions lacking economic substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The company intentionally omits Korean-source revenue generated from crew recruitment fees or disguises intercompany commissions as payments to a paper offshore affiliate with no actual service capacity, while the Korean entity retains effective control over the vessel management operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, Article 3 - the evader is liable for imprisonment of up to 3 years or a fine not exceeding 3 times the evaded amount, plus the underlying unpaid tax plus interest surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participated in the tax evasion are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax and interest, and may face criminal imprisonment of up to 3 years (up to 10 years if the evasion exceeds KRW 3 billion). A Korean court may also issue a travel ban and the director can be blacklisted for departure with a view to enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The crew recruitment agency conducts intercompany transactions with its non-resident parent or affiliates (e.g., crew payroll, placement fees, or exclusive business benefits) at unadjusted rates and fails to prepare, maintain, or submit Local File / Master File documentation within the statutory deadline despite exceeding the KRW 50 billion threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Tax Adjustment Act, Article 116, a penalty of up to 30% of the under-reported taxable income may be imposed (50% in case of intentional disregard), and in addition a documentation penalty of KRW 3 million to KRW 10 million per requirement. Transfer pricing adjustments can be made regardless of the foreign affiliate's profit rate, and secondary adjustments (deemed dividends) may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who fail to maintain required accounting records or give false instructions to omitting documentation are personally liable for the related underestimated corporate tax and surcharges under the Corporate Income Tax Act's joint liability rules. In serious cases, directors may be prosecuted for breaching the Framework Act on National Taxes, leading to criminal fines and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean subsidiary is a mere booking entity: it has no local office, no employees, no board meetings, and no substantive crew recruitment activity, but it invoices foreign shipowners for significant crewing services and directs payments to an offshore affiliate in a zero-tax jurisdiction, thereby shifting taxable profits artificially.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the former Article 17(2) of the International Tax Adjustment Act and the substance-over-form doctrine developed by Korean Supreme Court precedent, the tax authority may disregard the shell arrangement, recharacterize the income as attributable to the Korean PE, and impose up to 50% penalty on the additional assessed tax. If the shell structure is used to evade foreign exchange or licensing rules, the Maritime and Labor statutes may also trigger administrative revocation of the crew manning license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil will be pierced where the shell has no autonomous economic activity; directors are personally liable for unpaid corporate tax, employer payroll withholding obligations, and statutory crew welfare contributions. Civil restitution orders extend to the assets transferred out of the shell. Directors may be blacklisted (travel ban) and face imprisonment under the Criminal Code for fraud (Article 347) if they knowingly used the shell to defraud the tax authority.
